paragraphs: Niddah 21b, and Rashi explains: two Torah scholars from that place; and in Tosafot the explanation, from the Arukh, is that Zuza is the name of a sage. And in [Yerushalmi] Demai ch. 2, halakhah 1: Rabbi Mana said, I went to Caesarea — I asked Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elazar, and he said to me, "Thus Zuga practiced" — Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar in the name of Zuga of Caesarea.

notes.text: Rashi’s pair of scholars and the Tosafot/Arukh interpretation of Zuza as an individual’s name remain distinct. The notice’s Caesarea reports use Zuga.
